Vuelta 2026: Route and stages

Tadej Pogacar leads La Vuelta ahead of Ethan Hayter and Joshua Tarling. In today's stage, the riders head through the hills of Provence towards a false-flat finish, while tomorrow’s stage finishes uphill in the ski resort of Font-Romeu. On Tuesday, a compact mountain stage through Andorra awaits, after which the Vuelta enters Spain. The red caravan then gradually heads south before the race concludes in Granada on Sunday 13 September.

Follow today's stage live.

Discover the route of La Vuelta 2026.

Monaco – Manosque

Sunday 23 August - Stage 2 of La Vuelta covers 204 kilometres between Monaco and Manosque. Although the riders tackle only two classified climbs along the way, the route still features 2,630 metres of elevation gain. The finish is uphill.
Read more »

Gruisan – Font Romeu

Monday 24 August – Stage 3 of the Vuelta takes the riders over 174 kilometres from Gruisan to Font Romeu. The route features 2,676 metres of elevation gain, almost all of which comes in the final 35 kilometres.
Read more »

Route

La Vuelta a España packs 57,079 metres of elevation gain into a 3,298.5-kilometre route. The race starts in Monaco before gradually heading south towards the finish in Granada. Along the way, the riders face several brutal summit finishes, including Alto de Aitana, Calar Alto, Peñas Blancas and the monstrous Collado del Alguacil in the Sierra Nevada.
Read more »

Andorra La Vella – Andorra La Vella

Tuesday 25 August – La Vuelta does not dilly-dally. As early as Stage 4, a thriller awaits, starting and finishing in Andorra la Vella. It is ultra-short at just over 104 kilometres, but ultra-tough, with four climbs and a downhill finish on a route featuring 2,953 metres of elevation gain.
Read more »

Monaco - Monaco

Saturday 22 August – The Tour of Spain opens with an individual time trial through the streets of Monaco. The course is 9.4 kilometres long.
Read more »
